description: Read collections, NFTs, listings, offers and marketplace events, and search OpenSea's catalogue.

api.description: One OpenSea profile by wallet address or username, with its display name, bio, follower counts and verification flag. `is_agent` is a self-declaration, not a check by OpenSea.

fields.description: A wallet address or an OpenSea username.

api.description: USD value of one wallet’s NFTs and tokens, with profit and loss over a timeframe. Every figure is a string. `pnl_absolute` and `pnl_percentage` are absent, not zero, when the account has no history.

fields.description: Window for the P&L figures: `HOUR`, `DAY`, `WEEK` or `MONTH`. The API defaults to `DAY`.
Only value assets on these chains.

api.description: The chains OpenSea indexes, with each one’s symbol and block explorer. No input; the list is the valid source for every `chain` argument elsewhere.

fields.type: { chain: string, name: string, symbol?: string | null, supports_swaps?: boolean | null, block_explorer?: string | null, block_explorer_url?: string | null }[]

api.description: The NFTs in one collection, paged with `next`. Filter by trait with `traits`, a JSON array of `traitType` and `value` pairs sent as a string.

fields.description: JSON array of trait filters, sent as a string: `[{"traitType":"Background","value":"Red"}]`. Several filters are AND-combined.
Only NFTs with (or without) an agent binding.

fields.type: { identifier: string, collection: string, contract: string, token_standard: string, name?: string | null, description?: string | null, image_url?: string | null, display_image_url?: string | null, display_animation_url?: string | null, original_image_url?: string | null, original_animation_url?: string | null, animation_url?: string | null, metadata_url?: string | null, opensea_url?: string | null, creator?: string | null, owners?: { address: string, quantity?: number | null, quantity_string?: string | null }[] | null, traits?: { trait_type: string, display_type?: string | null, max_value?: string | null, value?: string | number | boolean | null }[] | null, is_disabled?: boolean | null, is_nsfw?: boolean | null, is_suspicious?: boolean | null, updated_at?: string | null, decimals?: number | null, estimated_value_usd?: number | null }[]

api.description: Floor price over time for one collection, as points carrying a float unix timestamp, a USD string and a token-unit price. Narrow with `timeframe`, and set how many points come back with `resolution`.

fields.description: Window to report, such as `one_hour`, `one_day`, `seven_days`, `thirty_days` or `all_time`. The API defaults to `one_day`.
Number of data points to return. The spec gives no default or bounds.

fields.type: { time?: number | null, usd_price?: string | null, token_unit?: number | null, symbol?: string | null, chain?: string | null }[]

api.description: One collection by slug, with its contract addresses, links and NFT counts. The answer is a bare object, not an array, and an unknown slug is a 404.
Wallet addresses holding one collection, with each amount and its share of supply as a fraction (`0.0127` is 1.27%). Sort by quantity either way. This route pages with `cursor`, not `next`.

fields.description: The previous response's `next` value. This route calls it `cursor`.
Order by quantity held. Defaults to `desc`.

fields.type: { address: string, quantity?: number | null, percentage?: number | null }[]

api.description: Collections, paged with the returned `next` cursor. Filter by chain, creator or hidden status, and sort with `order_by`. OpenSea defaults the page size to 50.

fields.description: The chain slug, such as `ethereum`, `base` or `solana`. `chains.list` returns the current set; OpenSea refuses a slug it does not index.
Only collections made by this OpenSea account.
Include collections hidden from search and browse.
Field to sort by. The spec types this as a free string and names no values.
How many to return. The API defaults to 50.
The `next` cursor from a previous page.

fields.description: Cursor for the next page; null on the last one.

api.description: Volume, sales, owner count and floor price for one collection, as an all-time total plus per-interval rows.

fields.type: { volume?: number | null, volume_symbol?: string | null, sales?: number | null, num_owners?: number | null, floor_price?: number | null, floor_price_symbol?: string | null }
{ interval: string, volume?: number | null, volume_symbol?: string | null, sales?: number | null }[]

api.description: Collections ranked by a metric, `one_day_volume` by default. This route pages with `cursor`, which is the previous response’s `next`.

fields.description: Ranking metric. The API defaults to `one_day_volume`.
The previous response's `next` value. This route calls it `cursor`.

api.description: Collections ranked by momentum over a window, `one_day` by default. Same page shape as `collections.top`, and it pages with `cursor` too.

fields.description: Window to rank by, such as `one_hour`, `one_day`, `seven_days` or `thirty_days`. The API defaults to `one_day`.
The previous response's `next` value. This route calls it `cursor`.

api.description: Search across collections, NFTs, tokens and accounts. Each result carries a `type` and one payload key, so branch on `type` before reading the rest.

api.description: The trait names on one collection, the type of each, and under `counts` every value with how many NFTs carry it (`min` and `max` for a numeric trait). Use `collection.nfts` with a `traits` filter to select NFTs by value.
